Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 28 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 93 % Which of the following is the most effective initial treatment at this time?

A 25-year-old woman non-smoker presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of severe chest pain and shortness of breath. Her past medical history is significant for caesarean section 4 days ago. Her examinations show a distressed woman with oxygen saturation 92% but otherwise unremarkable. Chest radiography is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 38-year-old man who is smoker for several years presents to the clinic with progressive shortness of breath. Pulmonary function test (PFT) done which results in the following parameters: forced expiratoy volume (FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio < 0.7 with minimal improvement after bronchodilators low diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman with a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) on combination of long- acting B2-agonist and inhaled glucocorticoid and albuterol as needed presents to the clinic with worsening of her symptoms. On physical examination, there is no jugular venous distention. Pulmonary examination reveals decreased breath sounds. Bilateral lower extremity edema is noted to a level above the ankles. Echocardiogram is normal apart of high mean pulmonary artery pressure, 52 mmH (see lab results). Blood pressure 125/75 mmH Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 86 % BMI 30 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values ABG PCO2 7.5 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.6 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 8.6 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment at this time?

A 66-year-old woman is evaluated for a 6-week history of increasing dyspnea and right-sided pleuritic chest pain with occasional cough. She has lost significant body weight in the last 3 months. She has no other medical problems and takes no medications. Her physical examination reveals dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds over both lower lung zones. A 4-cm right breast mass is palpated. Chest radiograph demonstrates bilateral pleural effusions but no evidence of infiltrate or pulmonary vascular congestion. Thoracentesis is performed. Pleural fluid Gram stain is negative (see lab results). Total Protein 40 10-20 g/L Fluid Protein/Serum Protein 0.67 <0.5 Glucose 3.5 >2.2 mmol/L LDH 350 <200/UL Total Proteins 60 60-84 g/L Lactate dehydrogenase 125 60-160 IU/L Leukocytes 3600 <1000/pL Which of the following is the most appropriate statement about the diagnosis?

options.text: Exudative pleural effusion due to malignancy
Transudative pleural effusion due to malignancy
Exudative pleural effusion due to heart failure
Transudative pleural effusion due to empyema

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with bronchial asthma that controlled on budesonide and albuterol inhalers is evaluated in the clinic as she is 6 weeks pregnant. Her symptoms are well controlled on the treatment. However, symptoms usually flare in fall and she treats these symptoms with an add-on oral leukotriene inhibitor. She currently has no asthma symptoms. On examination, vital signs are normal. The lungs show good air entry and no wheezes. She is so concern about the safety of medications during pregnancy. What is the best information to be delivered to her with regard to medication safety?

options.text: Continue the current treatments as they are safe during pregnancy
Stop budesonide and continue albuterol inhaler
Stop albuterol and continue budesonide inhaler

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and occasional wheeze that occurs several times per week. He develops significant shortness of breath when playing football. He notes that it takes several minutes to recover his breath when this occurs. He also notes coughing during exercise as well. He takes no medications. On physical examination, vital signs are normal. Mild nasal congestion is noted. His systemic examinations are unremarkable. A chest radiograph is normal. Spirometry findings are within normal parameters. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in assessment?

options.text: Helical (spiral) computed tomography (CT) for the chest

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is evaluated because of daily wheezing and breathlessness that limit her activities several times a week. Medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has never smoked. She is diagnosed with moderate persistent asthma. In addition to a short-acting 32-agonist, which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Add a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting B2-agonist

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with severe COPD is admitted with 4 days of dyspnoea and cough. She is alert, in moderate respiratory distress, and has an oxygen saturation of 93% on 3 L/min supplemental oxygen. A chest radiography demonstrates no consolidation. She receives intensive bronchodilator therapy and systemic steroids (see lab results). ABG PCO2 8.8 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.28 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 9.9 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best next step in the management?
A 58-year-old woman with acute onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain. She is diagnosed with pulmonary embolism. Which of the following is an indication to do thrombophilia workup?

options.text: Has a history of connective tissue disease
Has negative family history of thrombosis

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is evaluated in the clinic because of an abnormal chest computerised tomography (CT) scan that revealed a small lung lesion (7 mm) without any other abnormalities. He is non-smoker and he is asymptomatic. Physical examination shows no lymphadenopathy and normal lung examinations (see lab results). Hb 140 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 300 150-400 x 109/L WBC 8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 11 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Calcium 2.25 2.15-2.62 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate procedure to do next?

A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air. Chest examination shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most useful to establish a diagnosis of exudative pleural effusion?

options.text: Pleural fluid LDH >1/3 normal upper limit for serum

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air Chest examination shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following factors indicating the need for therapeutic thoracentesis?

options.text: Pleural fluid glucose more than 80 mg/di
Negative gram stain of the pleural fluid

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child with bronchial asthma seen in the clinic because of uncontrolled course of disease despite using Ventolin regularly. Mother has asthma and using similar inhaler but she expresses poor technique of Ventolin delivery to her child. Which of the following is the most likely reason for her child's problem?
A 5-year-old child with bronchial asthma under control with inhalers. Mother concerned about the future of her child's asthma during adulthood. Which of the following is the most likely prognosis?

options.text: Most of the children grow out of it
No correlation between childhood and adulthood asthma

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child with bronchial asthma on ventolin nebulizer at home as per needs. The mother expresses concern that the family cannot go out of the home most of the time because the nebulizer machine need electricity power source. Which of the following is the most appropriate counselling should be given?

options.text: Agree and support their decision as the priority is asthma control
Find someone to take care of asthmatic child if family goes out of the home
Educate with clear instructions inhaler usage and advice to stop nebulizer
Find out nebulizer machine with portability feature

questions.stem: What is the most effective treatment for moderate bronchial asthma severity?

options.text: Long acting beta agonist agents with steroids
Long acting beta agonist agents with anticholenergics

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy presents to Emergency Room with acute asthma attack responding to initial management with improved respiratory distress. His vitals after stabilization are recorded. The decision made for hospitalization. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 97 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 88 % Which of the following is the most likely reason for admission?

A 2-year-old child diagnosed in the Emergency Room with pneumonia. The mother gave history of poor oral intake and vomiting for whatever orally introduced. Clinically, the child looks well with no distress. Blood pressure 88/56 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 23 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following reasons justifies the child hospitalization?

A 3-year-old child seen in the clinic with fever and cough for 5 days following flu-like prodrome. On examination, he had decrease air entry and crackles over right lung middle zone. Chest X- ray is done (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 90/64 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 97 % Hb 12 165-195 q/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) Platelets count 328 150-400 x 109/L Neutrophils 80 40-60% WBC 22 4.5-13.5 x 109/L (2-10 years) 4.5-11.1 x 109/L (11 years-older adult) Neutrophils 84% (2.4-7.3 × 109/L) 30%-77% (2-10 years) (2.7-6.5 x 109/L) 40%-75% (11 years-older adult) Lymphocytes 15% (2.8-9.3 x 109/L) 26%-56% (Birth) (3.7-10.7 × 109/L) 20%-64% (1-23 months) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 2-month-old infant present to Emergency Room with cough, sneezing, circumoral cyanosis occasional with frothy secretion from mouth for the 3 days. On examination, she looks well with moderate tachypnea and intercostal retraction. Chest reveals scatted rhonchi and crackles all over but good air entry. Blood pressure 80/50 mmH Heart rate 138 /min Respiratory rate 48 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 91 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following sites is the best to aspirate a sample of right pleural effusion with a syringe and needle?

A 45-year-old man presents with difficulty in breathing and a nocturnal cough for the last 3 weeks. Spirometry results show a forced vital capacity and the FEV/FVC ratio lower than normal. Which of the following is consistent with these findings?
What is the optimal treatment for community-acquired pneumonia in an otherwise healthy patient?
What is the optimal duration of anticoagulation following an initial episode of pulmonary embolism?
In which of the following conditions is interstitial pneumonitis a characteristic histopathologic finding?
Which of the following pneumoconiosis will commonly predispose to the development of pulmonary tuberculosis?
A 38-year-old woman with pleurisy requires a thoracentesis. The needle should be placed on the midaxillary line of the affected side. Which rib level should the needle penetrate through?

A 72-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with fever, night sweats and cough for 2 weeks (see report). Chest X-ray: Right upper lobe consolidation. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options.text: Admit the patient to the Intensive Unit
Isolate the patient in a single, negative pressure room

questions.stem: Which of the following can improve survival in patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?

A 25-year-old patient with moderate persistent asthma is currently on a low-dose, inhaled corticosteroid but needs to use a beta-2 agonist rescue inhaler at least once a day. Which of the following should be added to the current treatment?

options.text: Leukotriene inhibitor to the steroid regimen
Long-acting beta-2 agonist to steroid regimen

questions.stem: A 55-year-old patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with shortness of breath. The patient is in severe respiratory distress and hypoxemic with decreased breath sounds and a prolonged expiration phase. There is no improvement with bronchodilators. The patient is conscious with a pH of 7.3. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
Which of the following is the most effective treatment for adults with obstructive sleep apnea?

options.text: Maintain a BMI less than 30 kg/m2

questions.stem: A 28-year-old patient with mild intermittent asthma, has daytime symptoms about once to twice a week, and none at night. Which of the following initial treatment should be given when necessary?

A 28-year-old woman has had mild intermittent asthma for years. She uses a short-acting bronchodilator, as needed. Over the past 2 months, she has noticed that she is using her inhaler at least 3 times a week, and on occasions has had to wake up in the middle of the night to use her inhaler. Which of the following treatments should be added?

A 55-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and a productive cough. The patient has a history of smoking. On auscultation, there is wheezing throughout the chest (see reports). Chest X-ray: Normal. Arterial Blood Gases: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient suddenly develops chest pain and dyspnoea. Vocal and tactile fremitus are reduced, and breath sounds are diminished (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows absent lung markings on the left side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely cause of lobar pneumonia in adults?

A 45-year-old man is admitted with general tiredness and fever. There is a past history of a chest infection of 4-week duration, for which he was given oral antibiotics. He felt better initially. but never fully recovered and is now becoming worse (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows a right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old nurse working in the pulmonary clinic, complains of fever and a productive cough for the last 3 months. She has received 2 courses of oral antibiotics, but showed no improvement (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and a cough productive of yellow sputum for the past 2 days. There has also been blood-stained sputum for the last 3 hours. The patient has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes a day for the past 35 years. On examination, there are rhonchi, wheezing, and crepitations heard over the right hemithorax (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.8° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Chest X-ray: It shows a dense infiltrate in the right lower lobe. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman with asthma has not had a severe attack for the last 3 months. However, she has a history of cough and wheezing 2-3 times each week. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 21-year-old woman comes to the clinic with episodes of shortness of breath on exertion for one year. She has to stop after 15-20 minutes of exercise, because of dyspnoea and coughing, which get better after about one hour of rest. There are no symptoms at rest. Physical examination and spirometry are normal. Blood pressure 125/75 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 12 /min Temperature 37.0° C Which of the following is the most appropriate inhaled treatment before exercise?

A 42-year-old man with asthma presents with daily symptoms despite regularly using a long acting -agonist inhaler and an inhaled high-dose corticosteroid. He also uses a short acting agonist inhaler as "rescue" medication. These episodes also wake him from sleep 2-3 times a week. Physical examination shows bilateral (see table). Blood pressure 140/85 mmHg Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.7° C Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second Normal value Before bronchodilator 65 % 25-75 % After bronchodilators 91 % Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Observe the patient using his inhaler

questions.stem: A 67-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and haemoptysis following a car trip for more than 5 hours (see report). ECG: Right axis deviation, an S1-Q3-T3 pattern, and a right bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old smoker presents to a clinic with progressive shortness of breath (see report). Chest X-ray: It reveals a massive right pleural effusion. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A 28-year-old patient develops the sudden onset of dyspnoea and tachycardia 5 days post a knee surgery. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with stage IIIB small cell lung cancer complains of new onset of back pain for the past 12 hours. Initial neurological examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action to take?

options.text: High dose IV corticosteroids and MRI

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man and current smoker, with 50 pack-year smoking history, complains of shortness of breath, dry cough and fatigue progressing over the past 8 weeks. The patient also reports a significant weight loss, corresponding to approximately 15% of body weight over the last 12 weeks. Physical examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient with active rheumatoid arthritis presents with pleural effusion. Which of the following is typical finding in the pleural fluid analysis?

A 40-year-old woman presents with recurrent attacks of dyspnea and cough when exposed to dust and perfumes. Physical examination is normal except for mild expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation. Which of the following tests has the highest diagnostic value?

A 44-year-old obese woman presents with sudden onset dyspnea. No cough, chest pain orthopnea or PND. History is significant for hemorrhoidectomy 2 weeks ago (see image, lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min ABG HCO3- 20 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.5 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.5 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 10 10.6-14.2 ka Chest x-ray: Normal except for the obliterated left costophrenic angle. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 30-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive dyspnea and dry cough for 3 months. No fever or weight loss. Physical examination revealed cyanosis, digital clubbing and bibasilar end-inspiratory crackles (velcro type) on lung auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man with poorly controlled epilepsy presented with fever, cough and left side chest pain for 6 weeks. The cough is productive of copious foul-smelling sputum. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and course crepitations in the right infra-clavicular area. Heart examination is normal (see image and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 39 °C Sputum culture: Mixture of aerobic and anaerobic organisms. What is the most likely mechanism for the underlying condition?

options.text: Direct extension from infected chest wall

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with bronchial asthma developed worsening dyspnea and cough following paint inhalation from neighborhood apartment. On examination, she is in respiratory distress, cannot complete a sentence and cyanosed. Chest auscultation revealed reduced breath sounds in both sides with short inspiratory and exploratory rhonchi (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Oxygen saturation 85 % ABG HCO3- 24 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 7.8 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.3 7.36-7.45 ABG P02 7.5 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best immediate action in management?

options.text: Nasal continuous positive airway pressure ventilation

questions.stem: A patient with poorly controlled bronchial asthma developed hypertension, which of the following antihypertensive medications is contraindicated?

A 60-year-old man with advanced squamous cell bronchogenic carcinoma presents with massive malignant right pleural effusion. He has been admitted several times with similar findings for which he undergoes several therapeutic pleural taps. Which of the following is the next best option in management?

A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough and reddish nodular skin lesion over both shins. On examination, she has palpable cervical lymph nodes and bilateral diffuse fine crepitations in both lungs (see reports). Chest radiograph: Diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates with bilateral hilar lymph nodes enlargement. Purified protein derivative (PPD): Negative. Cervical lymph node biopsy: Non-caseating granuloma. Which of the following is the next best option in management?

A 60-year-old man with post pulmonary tuberculosis bronchiectasis presents with massive hemoptysis. Physical examination shows coarse crepitations in the right scapular area (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
A 69-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on oxygen therapy for the last 5 years. Which of the following markers is most useful for monitoring the progression of this patient?

A 51-year-old woman with asthma complaining of increasing shortness of breath and wheeze in the past few hours. She has a long-standing diagnosis of asthma but her medication history suggests a lack of compliance. Her best peak flow measurements in previous consultations have been 300 L/min. Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in this patient?

options.text: Inability to complete sentences in one breath

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. His medication history suggests a lack of compliance. His best peak flow measurements in previous consultations have been 600 L/min. Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in this patient?

options.text: A peak flow rate of 250 L/min

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man, whose asthma is uncontrolled on beta agonist therapy, is commenced on a steroid inhaler. Which of the following is the most likely adverse effect?

A 58-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of breathlessness. He has been smoking all his adult life, he smokes 10-15 cigarettes per day. On examination, he has lost the nail fold angle of his fingers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man with multiple health problems presents to the Emergency Department with an episode of bronchospasm. He has a history of asthma and hypertension. He is undergoing a medication review. Which of the following medications is most likely to be responsible?

A 21-year-old man presents with paroxysms of coughing for the past week, following a mild flue illness. The paroxysms have been so severe that they have resulted vomiting and chest pain. He had been immunised for pertussis as a child. What is the best advice about the protection following immunisation?

options.text: Immunization offers lifelong immunity against pertussis
Immunity following immunization wanes within 3 years
Immunity following immunization wanes within 10 years
Immunity following immunization wanes after 25 years

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. He rarely attends asthma clinic and his previous best peak flow readings has been 400 L/min. Which of the following would suggest acute severe asthma?

A 38-year-old woman presents for annual asthma review. Her symptoms are very well controlled and she has not had any attacks since her last review a year ago and has not used her salbutamol inhaler once in that year. She is prescribed an inhaled beclomethasone steroid twice daily in addition to her salbutamol inhaler. What is the most appropriate next step in modifying her medication?

options.text: Double the dose of the inhaled corticosteroid
Stop both the salbutamol and beclomethasone inhalers
Half the beclomethasone dose and review in 6 months

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is admitted with a sudden onset dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain. He is a smoker but has no history of respiratory disease. He considers himself healthy and regularly plays football. On admission, he has a chest x-ray that shows a pneumothorax with a 3cm rim of air. Aspiration is successful and he is discharged. A follow-up chest x-ray 2 weeks later shows a complete resolution. What is the single most important piece of advice to reduce his risk of further pneumothoraces?

options.text: Arrange a course of respiratory physiotherapy pnemothorax

questions.stem: A 28-year-old wood worker presents to the clinic complaining of episodic shortness of breath. He describes feeling wheezy and having a tendency to cough. A diagnosis of occupation asthma is suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?

options.text: Serial peak flow measurements at work and at home

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man presents with shortness of breath. He smokes 20 cigarettes/day but is otherwise well. Spirometry shows a restrictive picture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old man came for smoking cessation support as his father has recently been diagnosed with lung cancer. He has a past medical history of epilepsy, which is well-controlled on carbamazepine. Which smoking cessation medication would be contraindicated for this patient?

A 57-year-old man with known history of asthma, congestive heart failure and peptic ulcer disease was admitted with asthma exacerbation and rapid atrial fibrillation. He was managed with nebulized salbutamol, IV digoxin, and his home medications was continued (ACE inhibitor, Ranitidine, Spironolactone). 24 hours later, his serum potassium is noted to be 2.8 mEq/L. Which of the following medications is the most likely to cause this abnormality?

A 32-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of generalized body aches, sore throat, runny nose, productive cough and shortness of breath. Chest exam shows right lung crepitations. The patient was admitted and according to the results of throat swab was started on oseltamivir (see report). Temperature 39 °C. Chest X-Ray: Right middle lobe infiltrate. Which of the following isolation precautions should be considered?

A 28-year-old woman G 4 P2012 immigrant presented to the Maternal Health Clinic at 20 weeks' gestation with a cough and night chills for the past month. The cough is productive and produces thick sputum. She had been prescribed treatment by a general practitioner for the cough and it had not responded to treatment. Patient nail beds and conjunctiva appeared pale and the cervical lymph nodes are palpable. Auscultation of the chest shows crepitation over the upper left lobe. She had received a BC vaccine as a child. A blood test is positive for interferon-gamma release assays. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.5° C oral Which of the following is the next best step in obtaining a definitive diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman with mild intermittent asthma presents to the Health Clinic at 24 weeks' gestation and says that her symptoms have worsened as the pregnancy progresses. Prior to the pregnancy, she had an occasional exacerbation of asthma and used only an albuterol inhaler for treatment as needed. However, she now complains of daily symptoms and once per week symptoms at night time. A forced expiratory volume in 1 second test shows 70% of normal. Which of the following medication regimen is now most appropriate?

options.text: Long acting beta 2 agonist and inhaled glucocorticoids

questions.stem: 116– A 34-year-old multiparous woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic at 28 weeks' gestation with coughing and difficulty in breathing. She appeared restless and uncomfortable. Auscultation of the lung fields shows bilateral rhonchi. The nail beds and oral mucous membranes appear pale. She is allergic to dust, pollen, mold and animal hair. There is no history of smoking. She reports that the symptoms began 2 days prior and had started with coughing up clear-colored phlegm. Blood pressure 124/72 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 37.5° C oral Which of the following tests is initially most appropriate?

An 82-year-old woman is admitted at noon with pneumonia to the General Medical Ward. At night, she is found disoriented and restless by the nursing staff. Blood pressure 152/88 mmHg Heart rate 99 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.2 °C Oxygen saturation 94 % Which one of the following is the best initial step the nurse should do?

options.text: Call her family to come and watch her at bedside
Restrain the patient physically in her bed
Orient the patient to her environment, start nasal 02 and raise the rails of her bed
Call the duty doctor for Lorazepam order of 5 mg IV Stat

questions.stem: A 19-year-old healthy woman presented to Emergency Room with left leg swelling and pain for 2 days. She has no significant past medical history. She just missed her menstrual period. Blood pressure 131/89 mmH Heart rate 92 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Oxygen saturation 94 % Which of the following is the most important question to ask next in history?
Which of the following is the main method for prevention of tuberculosis?

options.text: Treatment of the patients with tuberculosis

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man heavy smoker, presents with left sided chest pain and hemoptysis for 2 days. Recently his son has noticed change in the quality of his father's voice. On examination, he has early digital clubbing and both of his wrists are painful and tender. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 85 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 92 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 76-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He is currently taking salmeterol, using albuterol rescue inhaler 2 to 3 times per day for the past 3 months. He has been hospitalized for COPD exacerbations twice in the past 6 months. Which of the following medications should be added to the maintenance regimen?

A 61-year-old woman has had type 2 diabetes for 12 years. She takes insulin and d smoke. She was recently started on enalapril 10 mg daily for hypertension but coulc it because of a cough (see lab results).
 Blood pressure 160/95 mmH

A 37-year-old man presented to Emergency Department with a 10-day history of frequent vomiting. He was dehydrated, and his electrocardiogram showed flatening of the T-wave. Which of the following is the most likely acid-base abnormality?

A 32-year-old man presented with a 2-week history of frequent attacks of watery diarrhea. On examination, he was severely dehydrated. Blood pressure 90/45 mg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.2 °C Which of the following is the most likely acid-base abnormality?
A 61-year-old man with stable chronic kidney disease stage 3. Which of the following drugs is it safe to prescribe for this patient?

A 62-year-old man presents with progressive lower limbs edema for the last 4 months otherwise he is asymptomatic. He is known to have diabetes complicated with diabetic nephropathy and hypertension. His current medications are insulin, thiazide, ramipril and amlodipine. On examination blood pressure is 144/78 mmg, JVP not raised, +3 lower limbs edema with normal cardiac and respiratory examination. Renal function was similar to 3 months ago (see lab results). Sodium 138 (134-146 mol/L) Potassium 4.8 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Urea 12.9 (2.75-7.4 mmol/L) Creatinine 230 (44-115 mol/L) Creatinine clearance 22 (70-103 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

A 55-year-old man who has developed chronic kidney disease secondary to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is reviewed in the clinic. His renal function is deteriorating. Haemodialysis is planned to start soon (see lab result). Creatinine clearance 10 (70-103 mol/L) What is the preferred method of access to start Haemodialysis?
Which of the following scenario with acute kidney injury should be referred for urgent Haemodialysis?

options.text: Potassium of 7.5 after 3 courses of medical management
Patient who has had 10ml of urine output over the last 24 hours
Patient who has previously had acute kidney injury three times

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man has been admitted with abdominal pain and he need urgent contrast- enhanced CT but there is a concern regarding his kidney status as he has chronic kidney disease stage 3 (see lab results). Sodium 143 (134-146 mmol/L) Potassium 4.5 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Blood urea nitrogen 9 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 160 (44-115 mol/L) Which of the following is the most important step in reducing the risk of contrast-induced nephropathy?

options.text: Intravenous 0.9% sodium chloride pre- and post-procedure

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man comes to the Outpatient Clinic because of the recent development of marked peripheral edema. He has no significant past medical history. On examination, he has 4+ edema of the lower extremities (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 105/80 mmHg Test Result Normal Values Albumin 18 34-56 g/L Urea 5 2.8-8.9 mmol/L Creatinine 85 44-115 mol/L Dipstick analysis: 4+ proteins. Urinalysis: Oval fat bodies, and some hyaline casts and occasional RBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman is recently diagnosed as nephrotic syndrome secondary to minimal change glomerulonephritis after being presented with proteinuria. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment to reduce proteinuria?
A 30-year-old woman with Crohn's disease presents with hypokalemia refractory to aggressive parenteral and oral KCI supplementation. Which of the following is the next step in management?

options.text: Assess her serum plasma aldosterone to plasma renin ratio

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes treated with insulin. Recently diagnosed to have hypertension and proteinuria (see lab results). Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg Heart rate 87 /min BMI 29 kg/m2 Blood urea nitrogen 4 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 80 (44-115 mol/L) Glucose fasting 6.4 (3.5-6.5 mmol/L) HbA1C 7 (4.7-5.6 %) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 30-year-old patient presents with recurrent urinary tract infections, polyuria, and electrolyte imbalance (see report). Ultrasound: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple, variably-sized and thin-walled cysts distributed throughout the renal parenchyma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 58-year-old man with chronic kidney disease has been on haemodialysis for chronic kidney disease for the past 8 years. What is most likely cause of mortality in such case?
A 27-year-old man who has a sister with adult polycystic kidney disease came to screen for the disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening test?

A 70-year-old man presented to Emergency Department with generalized fatigability. 2 days ago, he had CT brain with contrast for possible transient ischemic attack. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Hb 170 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) Urea 30.4 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 378 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely mechanism for the renal impairment?

A 30-year-old man is found to have a repeated BP of 170/110 mmg. He is not on any medications. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Sodium 138 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 2.1 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 3.67 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 66 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 20-year-old man presents with hematuria, 1-day following a throat infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman is admitted with pulmonary hemorrhage and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. She has history of recurrent sinusitis and numbness in her right upper limb and left lower limb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and chronic kidney disease. presents to the Nephrology Clinic for follow-up (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 160/98 mmHg, Heart rate 80 /min Potassium 6.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Creatinine 440 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the best immediate step in management?

An 18-year-old man is complaining of red urine for 5 days. He has no abdominal pain and no dysuria, urgency or frequency. His history is significant for tonsillitis 3 weeks ago. Physical examination is normal except for elevated blood pressure. Blood pressure 160/100 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman known to have dilated cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 30% one month ago is admitted with a diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis. She had repeated vomiting and watery diarrhea for 3 days. Her urine output is reduced in volume. She is on furosemide, lisinopril, spironolactone, and carvedilol. On examination, she is dehydrated, confused, has cold clammy skin and the JVP is 1 cm above the sternal angle (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 88/55 mmH Heart rate 70 /min Sodium 142 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 5.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 230 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 220 44-115 mol/L Sodium 15 40-230 mmal/day Osmolality 1300 280-910 mOsm/Kg H20 Central venous line: inserted and is 3 cm of H20. Fractional excretion of sodium: 0.6%. What is the best option in management?

A 65-year-old man diagnosed with obstructing lower esophageal cancer and planed for surgery, patient is cachectic with more than 20% weight loss over 3 months. The treating team decided to start on preoperative TPN. Which of the following is the most expected electrolyte abnormality?

A 44-year-old man who was recently diagnosed as chronic kidney disease stage 4, presented to the clinic to discuss the diet in regard to his condition. He has read that potassium rich food should be consumed in moderate amount. Which of the following foods should he eat in moderation?

A 66-year-old man with hypertension comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He is currently taking a combination of losartan and amlodipine, which is failing to keep his blood pressure within target. Examination is unremarkable. His blood test and renal function profile were within the normal limits. What is the most appropriate next step assuming he has no relevant contraindications?

A 58-year-old man with diabetes mellitus came for follow-up. He is on metformin (Glucophage), 1000 mg/day, as well as atorvastatin (Lipitor), 40 mg daily for hypertipidaemia. There is no diagnosis of hypertension. His urine albumin/creatinine ratio is in the microalbuminuria range for the first time (see lab results). Blood pressure 128/77 mmH НА1C 6.3 4.7-5.6 % LDL (cholesterol) 2.1 <4.0 mol/L Which of the following would be most appropriate next step?

A 25-year-old woman presents with symptoms of extreme fatigue, no appetite, and bloody urine She developed a very sore throat 3 weeks ago but did not have it examined or treated. 3 days ago, she began to have bloody urine and swelling of her hands and feet. Her past health has been excellent. There is no family history of significant illness. She has no allergies. On examination, she has significant edema of both lower extremities. Blood pressure 166/108 mmHg, Heart rate 82 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old man with chronic and progressing renal disease. His GF is decreasing and most likely he will need dialysis sometime within the next year. Which of the following will be the most likely cause of death in his case?

A 77-year-old man with a history of ischemic heart disease is seen in the Hypertension Clinic. He is taking 4 anti-hypertensives drugs. Physical examination is unremarkable. Abdominal ultrasound shows asymmetrical kidneys. Blood pressure 169/99 mmHg, Heart rate 79 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most useful therapy to reduce stone formation in a patient with hypercalciuria?

A 50-year-old man presented to the clinic with recent onset of numbness of his feet and hands History revealed he has chronic kidney disease for 3 years. Examination showed decrease sensation to pinprick and vibration stimuli below the knee with absent ankle reflexes (see lab results). Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg Test Result Normal Values RBC 4 4.7-6.1 x 1012/L (Male) 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female) Hb 9 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 73 80-95 fl Potassium 5.3 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 46 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 674 44-115 umol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

A 64-year-old diabetic woman was recently started on hemo-dialysis through a femoral central line. During dialysis, the nurse notices that she is shivering. Detailed history reveals a 3-day history of fever. On examination, central line site was red with pus discharge. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?

options.text: Withdraw blood culture and start IV antibiotics
Start IV antibiotics and hold dialysis for 3 days
Withdraw blood culture, change the line and resume dialysis
Withdraw blood culture, start antibiotics and remove the line

questions.stem: A 64-year-old diabetic woman is receiving hemo-dialysis through a femoral central line. She develops line sepsis. Blood culture grows MRSA (methicillin resistant staphylococcus aureus). She was started on IV vancomycin 1000 mg every 72 hours (to be infused over 20 min). Immediately after starting vancomycin, she started to have flushing, redness and itching over the face, neck and trunk. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?

options.text: Stop vancomycin and label her allergic to vancomycin
Continue vancomycin but a lower dose
Continue vancomycin but slower infusion rate
Change vancomycin to cefazolin 1000 mg every 24 hours

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones reduces the water loss through the kidneys?

A 13-year-old girl presented to the clinic with fever and painful cervical lymph nodes. On examination, tonsils were covered by white exudate. Temperature 39 °C Which of the following is the most likely complication to develop?
Which of the following populations should be screened for asymptomatic bacteriuria?
A 29-year-old woman is diagnosed with rapidly progressive glomerulonephrits. Which of the following pathological changes is characteristic of this diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman is evaluated because of recurrent lower abdominal pain and diarrhea for the last 6 months. She also reported having occasional joint pains and a 3 kg weight loss. She received treatment with antibiotics, dietary restrictions, and antispasmodics without improvement. Barium series showed thickening of the terminal ileum and few strictures in the jejunum (see lab results). Hb 94 130-170 g/. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) ESR 85 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Which of the following is expected feature on physical examination?

A 56-year-old man presents to the Gastroenterology Clinic with frequent heartburn. He had upper GI endoscopy and biopsy, which revealed Barret's esophagus with low dysplasia. Which of the following is the best initial option in management?

A 60-year-old man with diabetes presented with progressive ascites, fever and weight loss for 2- months. Paracentesis revealed low serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man with HBV cirrhosis presents with increasing abdominal girth, lower limb edema, and 10 kg weight gain over the last 3 months. On examination, he has jaundice and moderate ascites (see lab resuits and report). Sodium 132 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 3.8 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Creatinine 65 44-115 mol/L Albumin 30 34-56 g/L Total bilirubin 25 3.5-16.5 mol/L Ascetic fluid analysis: showed an albumin level of 12 g/L and neutrophil count of 180/ul. In addition to salt-restricted diet, what is the best next step in management?
In a patient with ulcerative colitis, which of the following is associated with increased risk of colorectal cancer?

options.text: Colitis limited to the most distal 15 cm of colon

questions.stem: A previously healthy 22-year-old woman reports 3-month history of frequent bloody bowel movements with mucus and occasional right hip pain. She has had no history of contact with sick patient and no recent intake of drugs. Physical examination findings are within normal except for gross blood on rectal examination (see lab results and report). Test Result Normal Values Hb 110 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) MCV 72 80-95 fl Stool analysis: Shows many RBCs and few WBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman with no previous medical illnesses, presented with 7-day history of increasing jaundice, nausea, vomiting and right sided upper abdominal pain (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Total bilirubin 26 3.5-16.5 umol/L Aspartate aminotransferase 700 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 1650 5-40 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 126 39-117 IU/L Which of the following tests has the greatest prognostic value?

A 28-year-old woman presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain, loose bowel motions, and weight loss for 3 months. Colonoscopy and biopsy of the terminal ileum demonstrated non- caseating granulomas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain, bloating and weight loss. Physical examination is unremarkable except for BMI 18% (see lab results and report), Hb 90 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 70 80-95 fl Calcium 2.05 2.15-2.62 mol/L Phosphate, inorganic 0.79 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Tissue transglutaminase antibody: Positive. Which of the following is the best management?

A 56-year-old man presents with epigastric pain, bloating and weight loss. Gastroscopy showed antral mass and biopsy is taken (see reports). Helicobacter pylori breath test: Positive. Biopsy report: Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue lymphoma (MALToma). Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 36-year-old presented to the Emergency Department with a 9-day history of right iliac fossa pain, diarrhea and fever. He was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 10 years ago. Physical examination confirmed a tender mass in the right iliac fossa (see lab result and report). Test Result Normal Value WBC 17.6 4.5-10.5 x 10^9/L CT scan: Collection in the right iliac fossa (12x15 cm) with jejune-ileal fistula. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

options.text: Open drainage with resection of fistula

questions.stem: A morbidly obese 35-year-old with no relevant past medical history consults for weight reduction. Which of the following is the most useful to determine the most appropriate procedure?

A morbidly obese 23-year-old man complains of gastroesophageal reflux disease (see report). Upper GI endoscopy:Large hiatus hernia with grade III reflux. Which of the following is the most appropriate weight reduction procedure?

A 26-year-old man presented 3 days after a sleeve gastrectomy with left upper abdominal pain. Physical examination confirmed only mild upper abdominal tenderness with no sign of peritonitis. Blood pressure 100/70 mmHg Heart rate 116 /min Which of the following is the most likely explanation?
Which of the following is the most common cause of biliary colic?
Which of the following is most commonly associated with biliary colic?

A 52-year-old complains of left lower abdominal pain associated with passing loose stool and a loss of appetite. Examination confirmed left iliac fossa guarding and rebound tenderness (see lab result). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 98 /min Test Result Normal Value WBC 19 4.5-10.5 x 10^9/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 45-year-old patient complains of frequent anal itching, and post defecation pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man presented with a 4-hour history of sudden severe abdominal pain. He reports frequent use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for joint pain. Examination confirmed generalized abdominal tenderness and guarding with absent bowel sounds (see lab result). Temperature 37.8 °C Test Result Normal Value WBC 13 4.5-10.5 x 10^9/L Which of the following is the most appropriate initial imaging?
A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with celiac disease. Which of the following foods should she avoid?

A 25-year-old woman presented with episodic abdominal pain and altered bowel habits that have been present intermittently for the past year. The pain is "crampy." and moderate to severe. Defecation brings some relief, but she sometimes must pass several loose, watery stools before the pain resolves. She occasionally notes mucus in her stool and sometimes feels that evacuation is incomplete even though she is unable to pass more stool. Her body weight is stable. Abdominal examination are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to establish diagnosis?
A 38-year-old woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea develops tender red nodules on her shins. The findings are most consistent with which of the following?

A 28-year-old man with 4-months history of non-specific crampy abdominal pain and diarrhea alternate with constipation that is not related to any specific food. He has no history of food allergy. No history of weight loss. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, BMI 23 kg/m2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 30-year-old man with 3 years history of intermittent abdominal pain, bloating and diarrhoea is seen in the clinic. Which of the following complains is highly suggestive of irritable bowel syndrome?

options.text: Undiagnosed food particles in the stool

questions.stem: A patient that has been in the Intensive Care Unit for 2 weeks is receiving parenteral nutrition (see results). Test Result Normal Values Platelets count 250 150-400 x 109/L APTT 37 30-40 sec INR 2 0.8-1.2 Total bilirubin 12 3.5-16.5 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with GERD for 4 years on daily dose of PPI with a good control of her symptoms. However, she reported occasionally heartburn. She underwent endoscopy. which was normal. Gastric biopsy revealed Helicobacter pylori. She gave history of smoking 20 pack-year but she quit 3 years ago, but she gave history of social alcohol drink. On examination, she is obese otherwise normal. Which of the following risk factors is mostly contribute to worsening of her GERD and she should control it?

A 46-year-old man came to the clinic asking for advice about eradication of H.pylori. He is known to have GERD on daily dose of PPI for 8 years with good control. He developed new onset of epigastric pain and was found to have helicobacter pylori By ELISA testing. Which of the following can happen post H.pylori eradication in such patient?

options.text: Need to increase the PPI dose
Increase the risk of atrophic gastritis

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with a history of diabetic mellitus, hypertension and osteoarthritis presents with melena. He gave a history of NSAID use for knee pain. He underwent upper GI endoscopy, which showed 1 cm duodenal ulcer with bleeding vessel, hemoclip was applied with good hemostasis (see lab result). Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Oxygen saturation 95 % Hb 8.4 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

options.text: High dose of oral PPI BID
High dose of oral H2 blocker
IV PPI infusion for 24 hours then oral PPI
IV PPI infusion for 72 hours then oral PPI

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with a history of chronic alcohol intake presents with chronic dull epigastric pain and diarrhoea for 6 months. He reported 5 bulky stool a day (see reports). 72 hours stool collection: >42 gram of fat/24 hours. Plain abdomen X-ray: Showed pancreatic calcification. Which of the following is the most effective strategy to control his symptoms?

options.text: Diet modification with small frequent low fat meals

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presented to Emergency Room with 3-days history of epigastric and RT upper quadrant pain and nausea. He gave a history of fever and rigors for 1-day duration. On Examination, Jaundice and tender RT upper abdomen with no rebound (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 100/70 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Temperature 38.6 °C Test Result Normal Values Hb 11 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 16.4 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Direct bilirubin 49 1.5-6.5 umol/L. Which of the following is the least risk factor for cholesterol gallstones?

A 34-year-old woman presented to the clinic for evaluation of persistent high liver enzymes for 6 months. She is asymptomatic. She has no significant medical or drugs history (see lab results and reports). Direct bilirubin 1.1 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 1.9 3.5-16.5 mol/L Aspartate aminotransferase 53 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 43 5-40 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 546 39-117 IU/L Albumin 35 34-56 g/L US Abdomen: Unremarkable. MRCP: Showed multi focal segmental biliary strictures and dilation. Which of the following is the best next step in the diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man referred to the clinic with positive CV. He is asymptomatic with no history of drug use or previous blood transfusion. Physical examination was unremarkable, Reviewing of his lab test showed normal LFT with positive anti-HCV (ELISA), Hepatitis C RNA was negative. US abdomen showed normal liver. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
